summary: Acquire is a lean, almost puzzle-like exercise in timing: you place tiles to grow hotel chains and buy stock, but the real game is watching for mergers and maneuvering to hold majority/minority shares right before a chain gets swallowed. Turns are fast and rules are simple, yet the stock-value math and merger bonuses create surprisingly sharp, cutthroat decisions.
praised: Extremely clean, teachable rules that still yield deep strategic tension
The merger/majority-bonus mechanic feels clever and rewards paying attention to the board
Fast turns keep the game moving despite meaningful decisions
Holds up remarkably well as one of the earliest modern economic games
criticised: Tile draw luck can hand someone a dominant position or trigger a merger at a bad time
Can produce kingmaker moments where a losing player's merger choice decides the winner
Downtime and fiddly share bookkeeping increase with 5-6 players
Endgame timing (when to end it) can feel like a swingy, sometimes controversial decision

scoring.why: The winner is decided almost entirely by cash plus stock value, driven by who holds majority/minority positions in chains when mergers happen.
